topic: DP-3T: The Invisible Shield of Privacy in Contact Tracing
target_audience: University students (Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or Public Health Tech)

sections.title: The Privacy Paradox: Contact Tracing vs. Surveillance
lecture_lines: During pandemics, we need to track viral spread quickly.
Central tracking risks individual location privacy and surveillance.
DP-3T offers a privacy-first approach to digital contact tracing.
Can we notify exposure without a central authority knowing?
Meet Alice and Bob in our contact tracing example.
animations: Alice and Bob icons [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/user.svg] (#FFFFFF) appear in a park background.
A red virus icon (#FF0000) appears between the two users.
A central server (#00FF00) appears, attempting to track their location.
A blue 'Privacy Wall' (#0000FF) blocks location data from the server.
The text 'Privacy-Preserving Contact Tracing' (#FFFFFF) appears at the top.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Bluetooth BLE and Hashing
lecture_lines: Bluetooth Low Energy enables phones to detect nearby devices.
Cryptographic hashes transform data into unique digital fingerprints.
These hashes are one-way, making them impossible to reverse.
animations: Smartphone icon (#FFFFFF) broadcasts blue pulsing 'BLE' circles (#0000FF).
A yellow 'Secret Key' (#FFFF00) enters a gray 'Hash' machine (#CCCCCC).
A unique 'Digital Fingerprint' string (#00FF00) emerges from the machine.

sections.title: Step 1: Generating Ephemeral IDs (The Rotating Mask)
lecture_lines: Alice’s phone generates a unique daily Secret Key.
Hash functions produce rotating Ephemeral IDs from this key.
These IDs change every fifteen minutes to ensure privacy.
animations: Alice's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] generates a new yellow 'Secret Key' $SK_t$ (#FFFF00).
White formula $EpsID = Hash(SK_t || Time)$ appears on the screen.
The broadcast ID 'A1B2' changes to 'C3D4' (#00FF00) after 15 minutes.

sections.title: Step 2: The Digital Handshake (Local Storage)
lecture_lines: When Alice and Bob meet, their phones exchange IDs.
These IDs are stored only on their local devices.
No central server is notified of this brief encounter.
animations: Blue arrows (#0000FF) show Alice and Bob's phones [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] exchanging IDs.
Bob's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] stores Alice's ID 'A1B2' in a brown 'Local Log' (#8B4513).
A green server icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/server.svg] (#00FF00) is shown with a red 'X', knowing nothing.

sections.title: Step 3: The Diagnosis Report (Sharing the Key, Not the Contacts)
lecture_lines: If Alice tests positive, she uploads her Secret Key.
She never shares her meeting history or location data.
The server broadcasts infected keys to all system users.
animations: Alice's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] sends only her yellow $SK_t$ (#FFFF00) to the server.
Server adds $SK_t$ to a white public 'Infected Keys' list (#FFFFFF).
Bob's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] downloads the updated 'Infected Keys' list from the server.

sections.title: Step 4: Local Matching (The Privacy Win)
lecture_lines: Bob’s phone downloads the list of infected secret keys.
It locally reconstructs the IDs Alice would have broadcasted.
It compares these IDs against Bob's local encounter log.
A match triggers an exposure alert on Bob's phone.
The central server never knows that Bob was exposed.
animations: Bob's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] takes the downloaded $SK_t$ (#FFFF00) to recreate Alice's IDs.
The phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] calculates a list of IDs; 'A1B2' highlights in yellow (#FFFF00).
The brown 'Local Log' (#8B4513) opens, showing a matching ID.
A match is confirmed between the log and the calculated list.
A red 'Exposure Alert' (#FF0000) flashes on Bob's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg].
